heroData.title: EOR & PEO Services in Colombia
heroData.subtitle: Hire and manage local talent without a local entity
heroData.description: Navigate Colombia's complex labor laws with a professional Employer of Record. Ensure 100% compliance with 'Prima de Servicios', 'Cesantías', and the new 44-hour work week mandate.

steps.title: Documentation Gathering
steps.description: Collect the employee's National ID (Cédula de Ciudadanía), Tax ID (RUT), and educational certificates. For foreign employees, a valid work visa (usually Type V or M) is required before starting.

steps.title: Employment Contract Drafting
steps.description: Prepare a legally binding contract in Spanish. Options include Indefinite Term, Fixed Term, or Task-based (Obra o Labor). Fixed-term contracts must be in writing and cannot exceed 3 years initially.

steps.title: Mandatory Medical Examination
steps.description: Colombian law requires a pre-employment physical exam (examen médico de ingreso) performed by a certified occupational health provider to determine fitness for the role.

steps.title: Social Security Enrollment
steps.description: Register the employee with the Health Insurance (EPS), Pension Fund (AFP), Professional Risks (ARL), and Family Compensation Fund (Caja de Compensación). This must be completed before the first day of work.

steps.title: Equipment & IT Setup
steps.description: Coordinate the delivery of hardware. If working remotely, ensure compliance with Teleworking (Teletrabajo) or Home Office (Trabajo en Casa) regulations, which may require a small monthly utility stipend.

items.title: Working Hours Reduction
items.text: Effective July 15, 2025, the maximum standard work week is reduced from 46 to 44 hours. Employers must adjust schedules without reducing salaries. Further reduction to 42 hours is set for 2026.

items.title: Night Shift Surcharges
items.text: The labor reform shifts the start of 'night work' to 7:00 PM (instead of 9:00 PM) starting late 2025. Night work carries a 35% surcharge on the hourly rate.

items.title: Sunday Surcharge Increase
items.text: Sunday and holiday work surcharges will increase to 80% in July 2025, gradually reaching 100% by 2027. Avoid scheduling non-essential work on Sundays to manage costs.

faqs.question: What is 'Prima de Servicios'?
faqs.answer: It is a mandatory 13th-month salary bonus. Half is paid in June and the other half in December. It is equivalent to 15 days of salary per semester.

faqs.question: Can I hire contractors instead of employees?
faqs.answer: You can use 'Contrato de Prestación de Servicios', but if the person works under subordination, regular hours, and receives tools from you, the UGPP may reclassify them as employees, leading to heavy fines.

faqs.question: What is the 'Cesantías' fund?
faqs.answer: It is a mandatory severance benefit. Employers must deposit one month's salary into a chosen fund (Fondo de Cesantías) every February for the previous year's work.

faqs.question: Is insurance mandatory for EOR employees?
faqs.answer: Yes, ARL (Professional Risks) is strictly mandatory and its cost varies depending on whether the employee is office-based (Class I) or in high-risk environments (Class IV/V).

items.title: Regional Holidays
items.text: Colombia has one of the highest numbers of public holidays (Festivos) in the world. Plan your project deadlines around these frequent long weekends.

items.title: Social Security Portals
items.text: All EOR providers use the PILA (Planilla Integrada de Liquidación de Aportes) operators like Aportes en Línea or Compensar. Ensure you get the 'Comprobante' monthly.

items.title: Dismissal without Cause
items.text: Firing an employee without cause ('Sin Justa Causa') is possible but requires paying a mandatory indemnity based on the length of service and contract type.

steps.title: Gross Salary Calculation
steps.description: Include base pay, overtime, night shift surcharges, and any commissions. Ensure the total meets the 2025 minimum wage requirements (including 'Subsidio de Transporte' for low earners).

steps.title: Mandatory Deductions
steps.description: Withhold 4% of the base salary for Health and 4% for Pension. Apply progressive income tax (Retención en la Fuente) for salaries exceeding the minimum threshold.

steps.title: PILAR Filing
steps.description: Generate the PILA (Planilla Integrada de Liquidación de Aportes) file. This is the unified system for paying health, pension, and parafiscal contributions to the government.

steps.title: Electronic Payroll (Nómina Electrónica)
steps.description: Submit a standardized XML file to the DIAN (Tax Authority) for every payroll run. This is a strict requirement for the employer to deduct payroll costs from corporate taxes.

steps.title: Disbursement
steps.description: Pay employees via bank transfer in Colombian Pesos (COP). Most employees prefer receiving payments in two installments (Quincena) on the 15th and 30th.

items.title: UGPP Audits
items.text: The UGPP is the authority that audits social security payments. Mismatches between payroll and bank payments can trigger massive fines. Ensure every COP is tracked.

items.title: PILA Payment Dates
items.text: PILA payments are due in the first two weeks of the month, with the exact date determined by the last two digits of the company's NIT (Tax ID).

items.title: Transport Allowance (Subsidio)
items.text: Employees earning less than 2x the minimum wage are entitled to a mandatory transport allowance ($162,000+ COP/month). This is not subject to social security but is part of the Gross pay.

faqs.question: Is electronic payroll mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'Nómina Electrónica' is mandatory for all employers who wish to claim payroll as a deductible expense in their tax returns.

faqs.question: What is a 'UVT'?
faqs.answer: UVT stands for 'Unidad de Valor Tributario'. It is the standard unit of account for taxes in Colombia, adjusted annually. For 2025, 1 UVT is approximately $47,065 COP.

faqs.question: How are overtime rates calculated?
faqs.answer: Daytime overtime is 1.25x (25% surcharge), and night-time overtime is 1.75x (75% surcharge).

items.title: PUC Account Mapping
items.text: Every payroll item (Health, Pension, Surcharges) must be mapped to its corresponding PUC (Chart of Accounts) code to ensure seamless accounting integration.

items.title: Payment Frequency
items.text: While monthly payments are legal, the 'Quincena' (payments on the 15th and 30th) is the cultural standard and highly preferred by Colombian workers.

items.title: PILA Rounding
items.text: The PILA payment system (unified social security) rounds all values to the nearest 100 COP. Your payroll calculation engine must match this logic to avoid portal errors.

steps.title: Enter Monthly Gross Salary
steps.description: Start with the base monthly salary in COP. For 2025, ensure it is at or above the statutory minimum wage.

steps.title: Select Employee Type
steps.description: Choose between 'Dependent' (Full-time) or 'Independent' (Contractor), as social security split differs significantly.

steps.title: Review Statutory Deductions
steps.description: The calculator automatically subtracts 4% for Health, 4% for Pension, and applies the 'Retención en la fuente' based on 2025 tax brackets.

steps.title: Factor in Annual Benefits
steps.description: Toggle 'Total Cost' to see the accruals for Prima (13th month), Cesantías, and the interest on Cesantías (12% annually).

items.title: Salarial vs Non-Salarial Pay
items.text: In Colombia, you can designate up to 40% of compensation as 'non-salarial' (bonuses, meal vouchers) to optimize social security costs. This must be explicitly agreed in the contract.

items.title: Integral Salary
items.text: For very high earners (>13 minimum wages), you can use an 'Integral Salary' which includes all benefits (Prima/Cesantías) in one monthly payment. 30% of this is tax-exempt.

items.title: Voluntary Pensions
items.text: Contributions to voluntary pension funds (e.g., Protección, Porvenir) can be deducted from the tax base, significantly reducing monthly withholding for high earners.

faqs.question: Are transport subsidies included?
faqs.answer: Yes, for 2025, the subsidy is approx $162,000 but only for those earning less than 2 minimum wages. The calculator auto-applies this logic.

faqs.question: Does it calculate 'Retención en la fuente'?
faqs.answer: Yes, it uses the 2025 UVT value to calculate the progressive withholding for salaries over the exemption threshold.

faqs.question: Is the transport subsidy taxable?
faqs.answer: No, the 'Subsidio de Transporte' is not part of the social security base and is not subject to income tax withholdings.

items.title: Rounding Rules
items.text: PILA payments are rounded to the nearest 100 COP. The calculator applies these rounding rules to match official government portals.

items.title: UVT Updates
items.text: The calculator is updated every January as soon as the DIAN announces the new UVT value for the year.

items.title: Independent vs Dependent
items.text: Note that independent contractors pay 100% of social security on 40% of their gross, while employees split the cost with the company.

heroData.title: Entity Setup & Incorporation in Colombia
heroData.subtitle: Establish your business securely in Latin America's growth hub
heroData.description: From SAS formation to Chamber of Commerce registration, we handle the legal complexities of setting up your Colombian branch or subsidiary.
heroData.bestFor: Companies establishing a permanent presence in Colombia

steps.title: Drafting Bylaws
steps.description: Draft the 'Documento Privado' (Private Document) defining the company name, duration, object, and social capital. The SAS structure allows for flexible governance.

steps.title: Chamber of Commerce Registration
steps.description: Submit documents to the Cámara de Comercio. Pay the registration fee (~0.7% of the social capital) and obtain the Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation.

steps.title: Obtaining Tax ID (NIT)
steps.description: Apply for the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) at the DIAN. Initially, a 'Provisional RUT' is issued, and the final 'NIT' is obtained after bank account opening.

steps.title: Local Bank Account Opening
steps.description: The most time-consuming step. Requires physical presence of the Legal Representative and extensive KYC documentation. Estimated time: 2-4 weeks.

steps.title: Final DIAN Activation
steps.description: Submit bank account details to the DIAN to activate the final RUT and enable the issuance of electronic invoices.

items.title: The SAS Advantage
items.text: The S.A.S. (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada) is the preferred entity for 95%+ of new businesses. It requires no minimum capital and only 1 shareholder.

items.title: Legal Representation
items.text: Every entity must have a Legal Representative who lives in Colombia. Many firms provide 'Guardian' or 'Nominee' representative services for foreign investors.

items.title: Medellín vs Bogotá
items.text: Bogotá is the financial hub, but Medellín offers significant tax incentives for technology companies through their 'Valle del Software' initiatives.

faqs.question: Do I need a local shareholder?
faqs.answer: No, a SAS can be 100% foreign-owned by individuals or foreign corporations.

faqs.question: What is the minimum capital requirement?
faqs.answer: There is no minimum legal requirement for social capital, but $1,000 - $5,000 is recommended to cover initial bank account requirements.

faqs.question: How often must I renew my registration?
faqs.answer: Every year before March 31st, you must renew the 'Matrícula Mercantil' with the Chamber of Commerce.

items.title: Central Bank Reporting
items.text: Any capital brought from abroad into Colombia must be registered with the Banco de la República (Central Bank) using 'Formulario 4' to ensure legal repatriation of future dividends.

items.title: Digital Signatures
items.text: Getting a 'Firma Digital' for the Legal Representative early is critical, as it is required for all DIAN tax filings and many Chamber of Commerce procedures.

items.title: Notary Formalities
items.text: While SAS bylaws can be private, any property transfer or specific power of attorney (Poder) must be elevated to a public deed at a Notary (Notaría).

heroData.title: Staffing & Talent Acquisition in Colombia
heroData.subtitle: Discover and hire top-tier talent in Latin America's tech hubs
heroData.description: Leverage our local network to find specialized professionals in Bogotá, Medellín, and Cali. From executive search to high-volume tech recruitment.
heroData.bestFor: Companies scaling their teams in Colombia

steps.title: Sourcing and Advertising
steps.description: Post roles on top local portals like El Empleo, Computrabajo, and LinkedIn. For tech roles, Medellín's 'Ruta N' network is a critical sourcing channel.

steps.title: Technical Assessment
steps.description: Conduct standardized tests. In Colombia, psychological testing (Pruebas Psicotécnicas) is extensively used and often expected by local HR standards.

steps.title: Background & Security Checks
steps.description: Perform rigorous 'Estudio de Seguridad'. This involves verifying judicial records (Procuraduría, Contraloría, Policía) and educational background.

steps.title: Home Visit (Visita Domiciliaria)
steps.description: A unique Colombian practice: for many sensitive or senior roles, recruiters conduct a home visit to verify the candidate's living environment and family context.

items.title: The English Premium
items.text: Bilingual (English/Spanish) talent in Colombia commands a 20-40% salary premium over monolingual peers, especially in IT and BPO sectors.

items.title: Tech Hub Focus
items.text: Medellín has the highest density of developers per capita, while Bogotá remains the leader for financial and administrative roles.

items.title: Notice Periods
items.text: While 30 days is common, notice periods are rarely strictly enforceable in Colombia. Have a strong retention strategy ready for new hires.

faqs.question: What are the most popular job boards?
faqs.answer: El Empleo and Computrabajo are the market leaders for general roles, while LinkedIn is essential for professional and executive searches.

faqs.question: Are background checks mandatory?
faqs.answer: Not strictly mandatory by law, but highly recommended. The 'Estudio de Seguridad' is an industry standard in Colombia.

faqs.question: How long does it take to find a developer?
faqs.answer: Senior specialized talent typically takes 45-60 days to source and hire in the competitive Bogotá/Medellín markets.

items.title: Home Visits (Visitas)
items.text: Do not be surprised if local candidates expect a home visit. It is a traditional part of the 'trust-building' process in Colombian recruitment.

items.title: Net vs Gross
items.text: Always negotiate salaries in 'Gross' (Bruto) terms. Colombian employees are used to thinking about their take-home pay, but contracts must specify the Gross amount.

items.title: Trial Periods
items.text: Trial periods (Período de Prueba) cannot exceed 2 months and must be in writing. During this time, either party can terminate the contract without notice or indemnity.

heroData.title: HRIS & People Software in Colombia
heroData.subtitle: Streamline people management with local compliance automation
heroData.description: Manage employee data, leave requests, and performance tracking with HR tools that natively support Colombian 'PILA' reporting and 'Habeas Data' privacy laws.

steps.title: Requirement Mapping
steps.description: Identify needs for 'Nómina Electrónica' integration, time tracking, and self-service portals for 'Certificados Laborales' (Labor Certificates).

steps.title: Data Migration & Cleaning
steps.description: Migrate employee records, ensuring all RUT and Cédula information is accurate and standardized for PILA reporting.

steps.title: Local Compliance Configuration
steps.description: Configure leave policies (15 days vacation) and benefit accruals (Prima, Cesantías) according to current 2025 labor rates.

steps.title: Manager & Employee Training
steps.description: Train staff on the mobile app for clocking in/out, which is increasingly regulated for remote workers in Colombia.

items.title: Habeas Data Compliance
items.text: Your HRIS must encrypt personal data according to Law 1581. Employees must give explicit consent for data processing at the time of hire.

items.title: Electronic Signature Validity
items.text: Ensure the system uses 'Firma Digital' or 'Firma Electrónica' that meets Decree 2364 standards to ensure contracts are legally binding in court.

items.title: Mobile First Strategy
items.text: Over 80% of Colombian employees access HR tools via smartphones. Prioritize platforms with robust native mobile apps.

items.title: Vacation Tracking
items.text: Colombian law allows splitting vacations into 6 days of rest and 9 days of pay (monetized), or vice versa. Your HRIS must be flexible enough to handle these splits.

items.title: Workplace Harassment Logs
items.text: Companies must have a 'Comité de Convivencia' and track reports. A good HRIS provides an anonymous channel for Law 1010 compliance.

items.title: Teleworking Stipends
items.text: For remote roles, HRIS systems should automatically calculate the mandatory 'Auxilio de Conectividad' if the employee earns less than 2x minimum wage.

faqs.question: Does the HRIS need to be in Spanish?
faqs.answer: While managers might use English, a Spanish interface is highly recommended for employees to ensure clarity and engagement.

faqs.question: Can I use global platforms like Workday?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they souvent need a local middleware or 'plug-in' to handle the specific XML generation for DIAN (Nómina Electrónica).

faqs.question: Are salary slips digitalized?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'Desprendibles de Pago' are typically sent via email or accessible through the HRIS portal, and they must match the Electronic Payroll file sent to the DIAN.

items.title: Self-Service adoption
items.text: Enabling Employee Self-Service (ESS) reduces HR administrative ticket volume by up to 60% in Colombian companies.

items.title: Dian Integration
items.text: Automatic 'Nómina Electrónica' filing saves roughly 4 hours of manual data entry per payroll cycle.

items.title: Data Accuracy
items.text: Inaccurate data in the HRIS can lead to UGPP audits if social security payments disagree with the payroll accounting.

heroData.title: Professional Accounting Services in Colombia
heroData.subtitle: Maintain financial transparency and IFRS compliance
heroData.description: Ensure your books are kept according to NIIF (IFRS) standards. We bridge the gap between local accounting and global corporate reporting.
heroData.bestFor: Companies needing local statutory books and reporting

steps.title: Electronic Invoice Reconciliation
steps.description: Match all bank transactions against the XML invoices validated by the DIAN to ensure 100% tax deductibility.

steps.title: Tax Accruals
steps.description: Calculate and record monthly accruals for ICA (Industry and Commerce Tax) and Retención en la Fuente (Withholding Tax).

steps.title: Statutory Book Updates
steps.description: Update the mandatory 'Libros Oficiales' (Daily, Ledger, Inventory) which must be registered with the Chamber of Commerce.

steps.title: IFRS Consolidation
steps.description: Adjust local books (Group 1 or 2 NIIF) into corporate reporting standards for global headquarter consolidation.

items.title: Revisoría Fiscal
items.text: If your assets exceed 5,000 minimum wages or income exceeds 3,000, you are legally required to appoint a 'Statutory Auditor' (Revisor Fiscal).

items.title: Electronic Signature Manager
items.text: The Legal Representative and Accountant must both have active DIAN electronic signatures to sign off on monthly tax returns.

items.title: Bank Reconciliation
items.text: Monthly reconciliation is not just for internal control; the DIAN uses bank data to cross-reference reported income and expenses.

faqs.question: What are NIIF standards?
faqs.answer: NIIF is the Spanish equivalent of IFRS. Colombia adopted these standards fully in 2015, categorized into three groups based on company size.

faqs.question: How long must I keep records?
faqs.answer: Accounting records and supporting documents must be kept for 10 years by law.

faqs.question: Are digital receipts accepted?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided they are supported by the XML validation from the DIAN. Physical receipts are becoming obsolete for corporate tax purposes.

items.title: Software Localization
items.text: Ensure your accounting software handles Colombia's 'Plan Único de Cuentas' (PUC) and generates the mandatory 'Exogenous Information' (Medios Magnéticos) reports.

items.title: Expense Deductibility
items.text: Only expenses supported by 'Factura Electrónica' or 'Documento Soporte' are deductible for income tax purposes. Avoid physical or informal receipts.

items.title: Inventory Controls
items.text: For trading companies, the DIAN requires a detailed 'Kardex' inventory record. Inconsistencies can trigger a physical audit of the warehouse.

steps.title: SAGRILAFT Manual Drafting
steps.description: Create a risk management system for Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing. Mandatory for companies with revenue > 40,000 minimum wages.

steps.title: Appointing a Compliance Officer
steps.description: Designate a qualified professional (Oficial de Cumplimiento) who is registered with the Superintendencia and can sign off on risk reports.

steps.title: UBO Registry (RUB)
steps.description: Report all 'Final Beneficiaries' (individuals with 5%+ ownership) to the DIAN's RUB registry to prevent tax evasion.

steps.title: PTEE Activation
steps.description: Roll out the 'Programa de Transparencia y Ética Empresarial' to prevent transnational bribery and corruption within your local operations.

items.title: Late Filing Penalties
items.text: Missing a deadline with the 'SuperSociedades' for annual reports (Circular Básica Jurídica) can result in fines exceeding $50,000 USD.

items.title: Whistleblower Channels
items.text: Under the new PTEE regulations, companies must provide a secure, anonymous channel for employees to report unethical behavior.

items.title: Due Diligence on Partners
items.text: Always run 'background checks' on your Colombian suppliers and customers. High-risk sectors include real estate, gold mining, and agriculture.

items.title: Habeas Data law
items.text: Law 1581 requires companies to register their 'Database' with the SIC (Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio) if they handle sensitive personal info.

items.title: Conflict of Interest Registry
items.text: As part of PTEE, companies should maintain a digital registry where employees declare any potential conflicts of interest with government officials or vendors.

items.title: PEP Monitoring
items.text: SAGRILAFT requires enhanced due diligence for 'Politically Exposed Persons' (PEPs) and their relatives up to the second degree of consanguinity.

faqs.question: What is SAGRILAFT?
faqs.answer: It is the comprehensive risk management system for AML/CFT. It requires KYC on all stakeholders and reporting of suspicious transactions (ROS).

faqs.question: Does it apply to small companies?
faqs.answer: The full SAGRILAFT applies mostly to larger firms, but a simplified 'Régimen de Medidas Mínimas' applies to many smaller firms in specific sectors.

faqs.question: How often must I report to the RUB?
faqs.answer: Initially once, then updated whenever there is a change in ownership exceeding 5% or the UBO's personal status changes.

steps.title: VAT (IVA) Filing
steps.description: Bi-monthly or quarterly (depending on income) filing of 19% VAT. Automated through the DIAN portal using electronic invoicing data.

steps.title: Withholding Tax (Retención)
steps.description: Monthly filing of taxes withheld from employees and vendors. This acts as an advance payment on the annual income tax.

steps.title: ICA (Industry & Commerce)
steps.description: Municipal tax on commercial activities. Rates vary by city (Bogotá, Medellín, etc.) and specific business code (CIIU).

steps.title: Annual Income Tax Return
steps.description: Final settlement and payment of the 35% corporate income tax. Due in April/May of the following year.

items.title: Tax Treaties (DTT)
items.text: Colombia has active Double Tax Treaties with countries like Canada, Spain, UK, and South Korea. Use these to reduce withholding on dividends and royalties.

items.title: 4x1000 Bank Tax
items.text: Every bank withdrawal or transfer is taxed at 0.4%. Business accounts can nominate one account as 'exempt' for small amounts, but most corporate transfers will hit this cost.

items.title: Electronic Documents
items.text: As of 2025, 'Documento Soporte' (support document for purchases from non-invoicing entities) must also be electronic to be tax-deductible.

faqs.question: What is the RUT?
faqs.answer: The 'Registro Único Tributario' is your national tax registry. It contains your NIT (Tax ID) and lists all your tax obligations (Codes 05, 07, 15, etc.).

faqs.question: Are there tax-free zones?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'Zonas Francas' offer a reduced income tax rate (usually 20%) for industrial users and exporters, subject to investment and job creation requirements.

faqs.question: What is the 2025 UVT value?
faqs.answer: For 2025, the 'Unidad de Valor Tributario' is set at $47,065 COP. All tax limits and penalties are calculated in UVT.

items.title: Exogenous Information
items.text: Annually, companies must submit 'Información Exógena', a detailed report of all transactions with third parties, which the DIAN uses for cross-referencing.

items.title: RUT Maintenance
items.text: Ensure your 'Registro Único Tributario' activity codes correctly reflect your business. Mismatches can lead to issues with bank accounts or export permits.

items.title: Withholding Certificates
items.text: Companies are required to issue annual 'Withholding Certificates' (Certificados de Retención) to all vendors by March of the following year.

heroData.title: Contracting & Legal Services in Colombia
heroData.subtitle: Protect your interests with ironclad local contracts
heroData.description: Navigate 'Contratos de Prestación de Servicios' and Master Service Agreements with local legal context. We ensure your IP and jurisdiction are protected.
heroData.bestFor: Companies contracting services or white-labeling in Colombia

steps.title: Scope of Work (SOW) Definition
steps.description: Strictly define deliverables to avoid the 'subordination' trap, which could turn a service contract into an employment relationship.

steps.title: Intellectual Property Transfer
steps.description: Ensure the 'Cesión de Derechos patrimoniales' is explicitly stated in writing and notarized if necessary for software or creative work.

steps.title: Payment Terms & Surcharges
steps.description: Specify payments in COP to avoid FX fluctuations, or anchor to USD with a fixed exchange rate (TRM) date.

steps.title: Dispute Resolution (Arbitration)
steps.description: Standard practice for foreign MSAs is to include an arbitration clause (Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) to avoid lengthy local court litigation.

items.title: Labor Reclassification Risk
items.text: If a service provider works at your office, uses your email, and follows your schedule, they can sue for 'Contract Reality', leading to retroactive social security payments.

items.title: Notary Public Requirement
items.text: Some contracts and powers of attorney (Poder) require 'Diligencia de Reconocimiento' (notarized signatures) to be valid for third parties or government agencies.

items.title: Force Majeure in Colombia
items.text: Always include a detailed 'Fuerza Mayor' clause that specifically covers social unrest or significant legislative changes common in the region.

faqs.question: Can contracts be in English?
faqs.answer: Yes, but for government filings or court use, they must be translated by an official certified translator (Traductor Oficial).

faqs.question: What is the standard jurisdiction?
faqs.answer: Usually, for local contracts, the laws of Colombia apply. International MSAs may opt for Florida or New York law, but enforcement in Colombia still requires local homologation.

faqs.question: What is a 'Contrato de Obra'?
faqs.answer: It is a contract for a specific mission or task. It ends exactly when the task is finished, without a fixed calendar duration.

items.title: Electronic Evidence
items.text: Law 527 gives digital messages and emails the same legal weight as physical documents, provided their integrity can be verified.

items.title: Apostille Process
items.text: Any document issued abroad for use in Colombia (like a Power of Attorney) must be Apostilled in the country of origin to be legally valid.

items.title: Verbal Contracts
items.text: While verbal contracts are technically legal for employment, service contracts (MSA/SOW) must be in writing to protect intellectual property and define liability limits.

heroData.title: Software Solutions & Dev Teams in Colombia
heroData.subtitle: Build and scale your tech stack in Latin America's 'Silicon Valley'
heroData.description: Access Medellín's tech ecosystem and Bogotá's enterprise software market. We help you source, implement, and maintain custom software and SaaS platforms.

steps.title: Technical Discovery
steps.description: Audit local infrastructure needs, including cloud availability relevant to Colombia (AWS and Azure have significant local presence).

steps.title: API & DIAN Integration
steps.description: Ensure your software natively connects to the DIAN 'Web Services' for real-time electronic invoicing and payroll validation.

steps.title: Local QA & Testing
steps.description: Test performance across local networks (Claro, Tigo, Movistar) and ensure Spanish localization is culturally appropriate.

steps.title: Deployment & Support
steps.description: Establish local Level 1 support in Spanish to manage user adoption and troubleshooting during Colombian business hours (GMT-5).

items.title: Medellín: The Tech Capital
items.text: Medellín was named the most innovative city in the world and hostst the 4th Industrial Revolution Center. It offers massive incentives for software exporters.

items.title: Cloud Adoption
items.text: Colombia is a regional leader in cloud adoption. Most enterprise software is now SaaS-based, with local data centers improving latency across the Andes.

items.title: Software Export Taxes
items.text: Software exported from Colombia is generally exempt from VAT (IVA), provided it is consumed exclusively abroad. Proper contract wording is critical.

faqs.question: Can I hire a remote dev team?
faqs.answer: Yes, Colombia is in the same timezone as US Eastern (EST), making it the primary hub for nearshore software development.

faqs.question: What are the top tech stacks?
faqs.answer: Java, .NET, and Python dominate enterprise, while React, Node.js, and Flutter are the leaders in the startup and mobile space.

faqs.question: How are intellectual property rights managed?
faqs.answer: IP created under an employment contract automatically belongs to the employer. For contractors, a specific 'Cesión de Derechos' clause must be signed.

items.title: English Proficiency
items.text: While senior devs often have B2/C1 English, junior talent may need support. Many companies offer internal English classes as a benefit.

items.title: Remote First
items.text: The Colombian tech talent pool expects remote or hybrid flexibility. High-speed fiber optic is standard in major cities like Medellín and Bogotá.

items.title: Hardware Costs
items.text: Laptops and servers can be 20-30% more expensive in Colombia due to import duties (Aranceles). Consider sourcing locally for faster warranty support.

heroData.title: Marketing & Creative Services in Colombia
heroData.subtitle: Captivate the vibrant and digital-savvy Colombian consumer
heroData.description: From 'Influencer' campaigns to performance marketing, we help you navigate the unique cultural nuances of the Colombian market.
heroData.bestFor: Consumer brands and B2B companies looking for local growth

steps.title: Cultural Localization
steps.description: Adapt messaging to regional variations (Paisa, Rolo, Costeño). What works in Bogotá might not resonate in Barranquilla.

steps.title: Omnichannel Strategy
steps.description: WhatsApp is the king of communication in Colombia. Your marketing funnel must include a direct WhatsApp click-to-chat component.

steps.title: Influencer Vetting
steps.description: Collaborate with local creators. Ensure they comply with SIC transparency guidelines by clearly marking paid partnerships with #Publicidad.

steps.title: Media Buying & Optimization
steps.description: Budget for Meta (Facebook/Instagram) and TikTok, which have the highest engagement rates among Colombian demographics.

items.title: The Power of WhatsApp
items.text: Over 94% of internet users in Colombia use WhatsApp daily. Use it for customer service, lead nurturing, and even direct sales.

items.title: E-commerce Growth
items.text: Social selling is booming. Live-streaming commerce events are becoming a standard for retail brands during 'Cyber Monday' and 'Black Friday'.

items.title: Data Protection SIC
items.text: Marketing databases must be registered. Sending unsolicited emails or texts without an 'opt-out' and 'privacy policy' link can lead to heavy SIC fines.

items.title: Loyalty over Price
items.text: Colombian consumers are highly brand-loyal. Invest in community management and high-quality customer service to build long-term trust.

items.title: Festive Season Marketing
items.text: The Christmas season starts early in Colombia (November). Brands must peak their activity during 'Prima' payout dates in early December.

items.title: SIC Regulations
items.text: The Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio strictly monitors 'misleading advertising'. Ensure all discounts and terms are clearly legible.

faqs.question: What is the most effective social channel?
faqs.answer: For B2C, Instagram and TikTok. For B2B, LinkedIn is growing rapidly but professional networks still heavily rely on face-to-face or WhatsApp connections.

faqs.question: Do I need a local agency?
faqs.answer: Highly recommended for copy and cultural nuances. 'Colombian Spanish' has specific idioms and tones that global Spanish translations often miss.

faqs.question: What is the 'Día sin IVA'?
faqs.answer: It is a government-mandated 'Day without VAT' (19% discount). These days drive massive consumer spikes and require significant server and logistics preparation.
